title: KalmMind: A Configurable Kalman Filter Design Framework for Embedded Brain-Computer Interfaces
problem: Deploying Kalman Filter motion prediction from brain signals in resource-constrained embedded brain-computer interface systems. Limited optimization of KF for embedded BCI deployment.
motivation: Kalman Filter prominent for brain activity motion prediction but little effort spent optimizing for embedded deployment with power/latency constraints.
method: This framework helps you design custom hardware accelerators (specialized circuits designed to quickly run algorithms) that predict movement from brain signals using Kalman Filters. Instead of building one fixed design, you can adjust settings to explore different configurations—finding the sweet spot between fast response time and accurate predictions. This tunable approach is essential for embedded brain-computer interfaces that have limited computing power.
key_novelty: A configurable Kalman Filter hardware accelerator framework that optimizes the tradeoff between response speed and prediction accuracy for embedded brain-computer interfaces.
contributions: KF hardware accelerator design framework for BCI
Tunable latency-accuracy tradeoff via design-space exploration
FPGA-based improvements in both latency and accuracy vs state-of-the-art
limitations: Specific BCI electrode count, sampling rates, and other system constraints not discussed.
